summary: Chong Go is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Dongguk University and under traditional teacher Daehaeng Kun Sunim (attested 2012).
Chris Clark works in Buddhist studies and Indology. He completed his PhD at the University of Sydney under Mark Allon by 2015 and served there as an honorary associate (attested 2019).

Christian Bernert specializes in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the International Buddhist Academy and the University of Vienna, earning a Mag. phil. under Klaus-Dieter Mathes alongside teachers Junjie Chu, Karin Preisendanz, and Gerald Hödl.

Christian Coseru specializes in philosophy, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He was a fellow at the Asiatic Society (~1997–1999) and earned his PhD at the Australian National University (~1999–2003) under John Powers. Around 2006, he joined the College of Charleston.

Christian Gottlob Heyne (1729–1812) was a linguistics and history/archaeology scholar. He studied at Leipzig University (~1748–1752) and held a post at the University of Göttingen from circa 1763 to 1812.

Christian Haskett specializes in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology. He earned his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (attested 2010), having studied under Robert A. F. Thurman and Michael Chamberlain, and held a post at Washington and Lee University (attested 2010).

Christian K. Wedemeyer works in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He earned his PhD at Columbia University (~1993–1999) under Robert A. F. Thurman. His posts include the University of Copenhagen (~2000–2003) and the University of Chicago (professor since ~2003).

Christian Karl Josias von Bunsen (1791–1860) was a scholar in linguistics, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at the University of Marburg (~1808–1809) and the University of Göttingen (~1809–1813).

Christian Lassen (1800–1876) was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Heidelberg University and the University of Bonn under August Wilhelm Schlegel. He served at the University of Bonn as an außerordentlicher Professor (1830) and ordentlicher Professor (1840–1876).

Christian Lee Novetzke works in Indology, religious studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Macalester College, Harvard, and Columbia University (~1997–2002). He held a post at the University of Pennsylvania (~2002–2007) before becoming a professor at the University of Washington (~2007).

Christian Lindtner (1953–2020) was an Indology and Buddhist studies scholar. He completed his doctoral degree at the University of Copenhagen by 1982 and served there as a professor (attested 1980–1991).

Christian Luczanits works in history/archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Tibetology. He completed his Magister (1994) and PhD (1998) at the University of Vienna. His career includes posts at Vienna (attested 1995) and the Rubin Museum of Art as curator (attested 2012).

Christian Matthias Boehm is a scholar in Japanology, history/archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at SOAS University of London under the supervision of John T. Carpenter (attested 2005).
Christian Wittern specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. He has held academic posts at Kyoto University (attested 1993 as professor, and 2008) and at Hanazono University (attested 2011).
Christine Chojnacki is an Indologist who completed her doctoral thesis at Sorbonne Nouvelle University in 1991. She held a post as professor at Jean Moulin University Lyon 3 (attested 2018).

Christine Mollier is a scholar of Sinology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied under Kristofer Schipper. She served at the CNRS as a researcher (1989–1995) and director of research (attested 2006–2014), and as a visiting professor at the University of Chicago.

Christoph Anderl works in Sinology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics. He earned an MA at the University of Vienna (~1989–1995) and completed his PhD at the University of Oslo (~1997–2005) under doctoral supervisor Christoph Harbsmeier.

Christoph Cüppers is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Hamburg (~1974–1983), completing his doctorate under Lambert Schmithausen, and served as director of the Lumbini International Research Institute from circa 1993 to 2013.

Christoph Emmrich works in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies. He studied at Heidelberg University, receiving his PhD by 2004, and held posts at Heidelberg (attested 2001) and the University of Toronto as assistant professor.

Christoph Harbsmeier specializes in Sinology and linguistics. He studied at the University of Oxford (~1968–1972) and earned his PhD at the University of Copenhagen. He was a professor at the University of Oslo (~1985–2016).
